note: Real-Qwen run executed on a Colab T4 with the current code. DRAMATIC improvement vs run 1 (0/18 grounded): 6 concepts survived the gate (coverage HIGH), 3 hallucinated concepts correctly rejected, selected concept grounded, diversity 0.929. BUT the strict PLAN gate then rejected the selected concept's plan (coverage 26% < 55%) so NO plan was emitted -> verdict PLAN_REJECTED. runtime.selected_concept: The Clock That Never Ticks: Temporal Dislocation and the Illusion of Progress

concepts_human_eval: A 'The Clock That Never Ticks' (SELECTED): thesis is built on an INVENTED premise - a clock face stuck at 12:00 - but 'clock' and '12:00' appear 0 times in the facts. Its evidence_refs (scene-1/3/6 + 'another person partially visible', 'woman's face', 'looking around') are all REAL, so coverage HIGH. This is the demonstrated leak: real peripheral refs admit a thesis whose central object does not exist.

B 'The Revolver as a Symbol of Unresolved Violence': thesis names 'revolver' (0 occurrences), 'kitchen' (0), 'son's room'/*living room*; refs were 'looking around' (real), 'confrontation' (real, scene-17), scene-6 -> coverage HIGH but central object invented.
C 'The Light in the Window': window/snowy/subway-car refs are real (scene-10/13), but the narrative ('emotional descent of the father') is ungrounded - 'father' appears 0 times. Boundary case.
D 'The Car That Never Moved': fully grounded - car, garage interior, subway car window, car interior, burning car are all real objects in the facts. Strong.
E 'The Bench and the Dusk': fully grounded - dog (scene-2), bench (scene-3), arm (scene-14), riverbank (scene-1/2), rural road (scene-3). Strong.

F 'Anxiety in the Bathroom': mostly grounded - mirror (scene-14), snowy window (scene-10), woman's face (scene-13), convenience store (scene-6) real; 'father' in the thesis is invented. Good refs, slight thesis overreach.
rejected_concepts_human_eval: All 3 rejected concepts (Weight of Silence, Son's Choice, Father's Silence) had LOW claim coverage and were correctly rejected: 'kitchen'/'revolver'/'father'/'son walks to the front door'/'father enters the room without speaking' are not in the facts ('son' only matches as a substring of 'person', 'reason'). Rejection gate worked.
The claim gate now handles the run-1 failure mode correctly (father/son/revolver/kitchen concepts are rejected even when real scene ids are cited).

plan_gate_audit.reason: plan editorial_direction not sufficient after bounded corrective retry (strict plan gate)

main_problems: PRIMARY-NOW (plan): with concepts surviving, the STRICT PLAN GATE rejects the plan because the 4B model writes editorial prose from generic film vocabulary, not from the evidence scenes + PLAN_EDITORIAL_TERMS whitelist. No invalid plan leaks, but nothing is emitted yet.

SECONDARY (thesis-noun leak): the model writes invented star objects/characters (clock, 12:00, revolver, kitchen, father, son) into the thesis while declaring only real evidence_refs; the ref-level coverage gate cannot see the invented thesis subject. derive_refs must stop trusting declared refs for the CENTRAL claim, or the gate must require the thesis's salient noun to appear among resolved refs.
Fixed since run 1: generator now mostly reuses the grounded vocabulary; the run-1 hallucinated-family-drama failure mode is gone.
